messages:
incidents-bot: Pager: high error rate on /v1/generate across us-west-2 — impact: increased 5xxs and slow tails, paging oncall. https://status.internal/incident/1793456789 :rotating_light:
ashley: oncall acked, joining bridge in 2m. putting primary mitigations on the thread.
jordan: grabbing logs + spool of recent traces now — running a quick `gcloud logging read` grouped by instance id. will paste queries.
kai: seeing elevated token-latency and a spike in KV cache miss rate in the runtime metrics dashboard. not sure if it's a routing issue or model OOM.
devin: any customer-facing impact so we can decide status page severity?
ashley: initial check: 4 external customers reported degraded generation and partial failures. not full outage but error rate >5% for 10+ minutes. recommend status page "degraded performance" for affected endpoints.
priya: +1 on degraded performance. I'll draft the status message once we have a concise root cause hypothesis. assigning comms to emma-commms unless she objects.
emma-commms: I can draft now. need exact affected endpoints, duration window, and mitigation steps.
ops-bot: Bridge created: https://meet.internal/bridge/1793456789. Incident channel set to #incidents. Incident severity: S2.
jordan: pasted log query: ```gcloud logging read 'resource.type="k8s_container" AND jsonPayload.service="runtime" AND timestamp>="2026-03-15T16:00:00Z"' --limit 5000``` putting results to /logs/1793456789/trace-snippet.json (s3://redwood-logs/1793456789/).
kai: copy of runtime metric where KV miss rate spikes: `http://grafana/internal/d/runtime/kv-miss?start=now-30m&end=now` — looks like cache invalidation events around 2026-03-15T16:08Z.
devin: hypothesis A: upstream rollout toggled a cache key eviction policy -> sudden miss storm -> increased inference CPU and > latency -> some requests timed out and retried causing downstream 5xxs.
ashley: hypothesis B: autoscaler glitch on dedicated pools in us-west-2 causing routing to fallback to cold instances -> KV cache warmed poorly -> same symptom.
priya: both plausible. we need timeline: when did cache invalidations start, when autoscaling events occurred, and customer-facing errors first reported. jordan, can you correlate traces with autoscaler logs?
jordan: on it. initial join: autoscaler shows scale-down + scale-up activity around 16:07Z for nodepool-rt-usw2. attaching excerpt: ```[2026-03-15T16:06:52Z] scaleDown starting node-rt-17
[2026-03-15T16:07:30Z] scaleUp requested node-rt-24 due to CPU spike
[2026-03-15T16:08:05Z] node-rt-24 ready
```
sam: I pulled the request-level logs and see a pattern: increased 504s correspond with requests routed to node-rt-24 during warm-up window 16:07:30-16:12:00Z. latency tails are high.
kai: also note a spike in model KV eviction events at 16:06:40Z across 3 racks. those line up with the autoscale window. could be cascade: eviction -> spike -> autoscale -> cold nodes -> more misses.
devin: ok so mitigation: 1) force route traffic to healthy warm pool in us-east until we confirm stability 2) enable temporary sticky routing to avoid cross-pool churn 3) roll back any recent cache eviction config if found. who can execute routing change?
ashley: I can apply a routing rule to route 100% of non-low-priority traffic to us-east for the next 30m. doing that now, will post confirmation.
ashley: routing change applied -> traffic routed to us-east for non-committed customers. monitoring for error rate drop.
priya: Emma, draft suggestion for status page: short template below — please adapt: 
```
We are investigating degraded performance for the generation API in us-west-2. Customers may experience increased latency and intermittent failures. Our mitigations are in progress. We'll post updates at 15-minute intervals. Impact window started ~2026-03-15T16:06Z. Affected customers: subset of hosted API users. Assigned engineer: ashley. For questions, contact support@redwood.ai.
```
emma-commms: copying that into status page draft now. will publish once we confirm error trend improving or at next 15-min tick.
jordan: attaching correlation CSV to /logs/1793456789/correlation.csv (s3 link) — includes per-request node id, timestamp, latency, response code.
ashley: after routing change, errors dropped ~70% in the first 3 minutes. still seeing some tails but much improved.
priya: OK start stakeholder notification: product-ops, sales leads, and account execs for the affected customers. I can send an internal digest: who/when/what.
product-ops: please include the customer list and the timeline summary. I will prepare a standup note for the execs at 16:45Z.
sam: adding a short in-thread checklist for the RCA capture (so we don't lose context):
- collect autoscaler events (jordan)
- collect runtime eviction logs (kai)
- collect request traces + customer impact mapping (jordan + sam)
- confirm recent infra/config changes (infra team)
- preserve logs and tag with incident id (ops-bot)
- draft timeline entries with who/when/what (ashley/priya)

I'll update the timeline as we confirm entries.
priya: for the status page update cadence: publish initial (draft) now -> update at 16:30Z with mitigation status -> final update when all services stable. Emma, set the published message to 'Investigating' now, then update to 'Identified' once root cause is confirmed.
emma-commms: published initial status (Investigating) and included approximate impact window. Next update scheduled 16:30Z.
ashley: adding timeline note: 16:06Z — KV eviction spike begins; 16:07Z — autoscaler scale-down/up activity; 16:08Z — node-rt-24 comes online; 16:09Z — customer errors increase; 16:13Z — routing change applied to us-east; 16:16Z — error rate dropped ~70%.
priya: assigning owners: timeline drafting = ashley, logs correlation = jordan, RCA writeup = sam + kai, customer-facing notes = emma, internal exec summary = product-ops.
kai: quick note on hypotheses: mark A=cache-config-eviction, B=autoscaler-churn, C=hot-spot traffic from single org. we should validate C by filtering traces by org id. jordan, can you add org-id breakdown?
jordan: yep running breakdown now, will upload table. preliminary: 3rd-party integration org-662 accounted for ~42% of the traffic spike between 16:05-16:10Z.
devin: that strengthens hypothesis C as contributing factor. might be traffic pattern plus eviction policy -> amplification.
priya: next comms steps: internal exec note at 16:45Z (product-ops), detailed postmortem timeline draft by EOD (sam/kai), customer follow-up email for affected accounts in 24h (sales+support).
emma-commms: will schedule customer email draft ready for review in 3 hours.
ops-bot: Logs archived with tag incident:1793456789. retention export completed.
ashley: leaving bridge but will monitor. if error rate creeps back, will re-open routing. thanks all.
priya: great work — keeping this thread as the single source of truth for timeline entries. please paste any final artifacts (queries, CSVs, screenshots) here before we close the live incident.
product-ops: noted. I'll compile the exec digest once timeline is finalized.
sam: adding final note: preliminary root cause: cascade between sudden KV evictions and autoscaler churn amplified by concentrated traffic from org-662. marking incident as mitigated for now; RCA in progress.
ashley: confirmed mitigated at 16:18Z, monitoring until 17:00Z then will move to recovery phase.
priya: closing actions checklist (in-thread): logs preserved, owners assigned, status page updates scheduled, customer comms drafted. if no further regressions we can transition to postmortem.
incidents-bot: Incident 1793456789 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. incident channel will stay open for postmortem artifacts. :white_check_mark:
